tools.name: bb_search
tools.description: Unified indexed retrieval for symbol lists, content, exact symbol source, or files. This is retrieval, not natural-language explanation or code analysis. `symbols` (default) searches indexed symbol NAMES with exact, prefix and substring phases, optional case folding (default: case-insensitive over every Unicode case pair), exact-name restriction, regex name matching (the query is then a JavaScript RegExp source, validated and bounded), language/symbolKind filters (case-insensitive against the indexed vocabulary), snippets and paging; it answers as text lines plus a final machine-readable match-set line (`[match-set] searchMode=symbols totalMatches=… returned=… truncated=… staleCount=…`) so a short page is never read as a complete one. `content` searches the indexed symbol corpus — name, qualified name, docstring and the stored bounded symbol body — case-insensitively, and answers as JSON declaring the match set (`total`, `returned`, `truncated`, `truncationReason`), HOW it matched (`matchMode` phrase when the query appeared verbatim, terms when nothing matched verbatim and the query's content words were matched instead, with `termMatch` naming which words carried the best hit), `bodyCoverage` ({ withBody, symbols, ratio }) so 'nothing matched' is distinguishable from 'nothing could match', and a freshness block. `symbol` returns the exact indexed symbol record(s) with byte bounds, language and per-match freshness, declaring `found` and `totalMatches` (the complete match set; this mode has no paging). `file` returns current source for one indexed project-relative file, bounded to 100,000 characters with `contentLength`/`truncated` and a file-scoped freshness block; it never auto-refreshes. `symbol`, `content` and `symbols` modes auto-refresh stale files they touch within a bounded budget and declare the decision in an `autoRefresh` field; `refresh:false` opts out. Stale rows carry `stale:true` and the freshness block's remediation names the manual reindex command (file scope names that exact file). `limit` is a page size and a work budget: 0 returns no rows, values above 2000 are refused rather than clamped, and `limit`/`offset` are accepted only by the modes that page (`symbols`, `content`). `language`/`symbolKind` values the index does not contain are errors naming the indexed vocabulary; options a mode cannot honour are refused naming that mode's accepted set; an invalid regex is a named error; a candidate cap, projection cap or time budget is reported as `truncated` with `truncationReason` instead of a complete-looking page.

query.description: symbol/content/regex query, trimmed before use; also accepted as the exact symbol name in symbol mode. Not accepted in file mode

symbolName.description: exact symbol name for symbol mode; supplying it with a different query is an error

filePath.description: file target for file mode, or symbol disambiguation in symbol mode. Not accepted in symbols/content modes

limit.description: max results (default 15; 0 returns no rows; above 2000 is refused; whole number). symbols/content modes page; symbol mode returns the COMPLETE match set when omitted and pages when given (its `totalMatches` is always the complete set size)

language.description: filter by language, case-insensitive (e.g. typescript, python, go); a language this project does not index is an error. symbols/content modes only

symbolKind.description: filter by symbol kind, case-insensitive (function, class, variable, interface, enum, ...); a kind this project does not index is an error. symbols/content modes only

includeContent.description: include a code snippet per result (default false). symbols mode only

exact.description: only exact name matches (default false); obeys caseSensitive. symbols mode only

caseSensitive.description: case-sensitive matching (default false); folds every Unicode case pair, not only ASCII. symbols mode only

regex.description: treat query as a regex against symbol names (default false). symbols mode only

offset.description: pagination offset (default 0). symbols/content modes, and symbol mode when `limit` is given

refresh.description: false opts out of the inline auto-refresh of stale files (default: auto-refresh within budget before answering). Accepted by symbols/content/symbol; file mode never auto-refreshes and does not accept it

documentation.summary: Unified lexical, content, exact-symbol, and file retrieval.

returns: `symbols` mode: one text line per match (name [kind] file:line (language), plus a snippet when includeContent is set) and a final machine-readable `[match-set] searchMode=symbols totalMatches=… returned=… truncated=… staleCount=…` line

`content` mode: JSON with the match set (`total`, `returned`, `truncated`, optional `truncationReason`), the route (`matchMode` phrase/terms, `termMatch` on the terms route), `bodyCoverage`, page-local `staleCount`/`freshCount`/`pageStaleCount`, and a `freshness` block

`symbol` mode: JSON `matches` of exact indexed symbol records (id, fileId, name, symbolType, lineStart, byteStart, byteEnd, language), `found`, `totalMatches`, `returned`/`truncated` when paged, per-match `stale`, and a `freshness` block

`file` mode: JSON source envelope (`searchMode`, project-relative `file`, `fileId`, `language`, `content`, `contentLength`, `truncated` at 100,000 characters, `totalMatches: 1`, `stale`) plus a file-scoped `freshness` block
errors: Missing or blank mode-specific query, symbolName or filePath
Invalid regular expression: a named error carrying the pattern and the engine's reason
`exact` combined with `regex` in symbols mode (they ask for different things)
`limit` above 2000: refused, never clamped
`language`/`symbolKind` value the index does not contain: the message names the indexed vocabulary
Option that the chosen mode cannot honour: the message names that mode's accepted set
Project has no index: the message names the reindex command
File mode: path escapes the project root, path is not a file, or the file is not indexed
limitations: Content search is lexical over the indexed symbol corpus (name, qualified name, docstring and the stored bounded body). It is not full-text file search and it is not semantic — use bb_ask for semantic discovery.

A body-only word is unreachable when the index was built by an analyzer that does not store symbol bodies. `bodyCoverage` reports how much of the corpus carries a searchable body so 'nothing matched' is distinguishable from 'nothing could match'.
Regex matching scans at most 20,000 candidate symbol names under a 2,000 ms matching budget. A cut scan is reported as `truncated` with `truncationReason` and is never presented as a complete answer.
`symbol` mode returns the complete match set unless `limit` is given; with `limit` it pages over that complete set (`totalMatches` always names the whole set).
Results reflect the index and may be stale. Stale/missing files are flagged per row and in the freshness block, and the remediation names the manual reindex command.
tools.performance: Indexed name lookup (symbols/symbol) is bounded by a candidate cap that scales with the page and answers in milliseconds on small projects and within seconds on a 310,423-symbol index. Content mode runs bounded candidate phases on projects large enough for them and a single ranked corpus pass otherwise; neither is a full-text file scan. Regex scans are hard-bounded by the candidate cap and the matching budget. Measured warm on a 6,452-file / 310,423-symbol index: symbols p95 3.6 s, content p95 3.3 s, symbol p95 29 ms, file p95 38 ms.
tools.safety: No source file is ever modified. `symbols`/`content`/`symbol` reindex stale files they touch within a bounded budget unless BB_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1 or refresh=false (declared in `autoRefresh`); `file` never auto-refreshes. A content read does not persist schema in the index database: the durable search index is built by maintenance, and the ranking table a query needs is created in the connection's temp schema.
tools.evidence: Paths, line ranges, symbol kinds, byte bounds and snippets are indexed evidence; per-row `stale` flags plus the freshness block qualify it. In content mode `matchMode`/`termMatch` say whether a hit is a verbatim phrase or a keyword coincidence, and `bodyCoverage` says how much of the corpus could match at all.

tools.name: bb_ask
tools.description: Answer a question about the codebase from the index, with the route and its limits stated. Four routes: (1) an EXACT AGGREGATE over indexed rows (counts of symbols/functions/classes/interfaces/structs/enums/traits/types/constants/relationships/imports/files, optionally by language; the largest file; the most complex function) — exact about the indexed snapshot, with that snapshot's time reported, and never a similarity claim; (2) an EXACT SYMBOL NAME lookup when the query is a single symbol name — matched by name, not by similarity, with its neighbours listed and labelled as neighbours; (3) SEMANTIC RETRIEVAL over stored embeddings — only vectors from the same model and dimension as the query are compared, similarities are cosine scores, and the answer reports which model space it compared, how many symbols exist in that space versus across the whole library, whether the scan cap was reached, and whether the provider embedding timed out (then a capped local 50-dimension fallback runs); (4) a KEYWORD FALLBACK when embeddings are unavailable or nothing clears the similarity floor — lexical matches that carry NO similarity score, with the reason stated. Every answer reports its confidence kind: a mean of returned similarities (bounded 0.2–0.85), a declared floor when no score was computed, or NO confidence number at all when the ranking is declared non-discriminative (the answer then says the scores do not separate candidates). Every answer declares `returned`/`totalMatches`/`truncated` bounds so a prefix is never read as a complete match set. Cited sources carry `[STALE — file changed since index]` or `[MISSING — file no longer on disk]` markers, and nothing is auto-refreshed. `limit` is the page size: whole number 1..100, default 5, values outside refused rather than clamped. When embeddings are configured, the natural-language question itself is sent to the configured embedding provider to compute the query vector; with local word vectors everything stays offline.

query.description: natural-language question, or a symbol name for the exact-name route

limit.description: max results (default 5; whole number 1..100; values outside are refused, not clamped). A larger page also means a larger work budget.

documentation.summary: Exact aggregates, exact-name lookups, and scored semantic or lexical matches — each labelled with its route and bounds.

examples.query: how many functions are in this project

returns: Exact aggregates over the indexed snapshot — symbol counts by kind (functions count both `function`- and `method`-kind symbols), relationships, imports, files (optionally by language), the largest file and the most complex function — each answer carrying the index snapshot's timestamp
An exact symbol-name lookup when the query is a symbol name, with its neighbours listed and explicitly labelled as neighbours rather than better matches

Ranked semantic matches with real cosine similarities when stored embeddings allow it, each answer naming the compared model, the symbols comparable in that model space, the library-wide coverage, the scan bounds, and per-source `[STALE — file changed since index]` / `[MISSING — file no longer on disk]` markers
Lexical matches when embeddings are unavailable or nothing clears the similarity floor — with NO similarity number printed, because none was computed, and the fallback reason named

Declared bounds on every answer: `returned`, `totalMatches` (or an explicit unknown), `truncated` and `truncationReason`; plus a confidence kind: exact aggregate, exact name lookup, mean of returned similarities (bounded 0.2–0.85), declared floor, or none when the ranking is declared non-discriminative
errors: Empty or whitespace-only query
`limit` outside 1..100 (0 included) — refused rather than clamped, because a clamped page looks like the page the caller asked for
Unknown option, or a mode that exists only in `plannedModes` (`explain`, `feature`)
No index for the project, or an index that cannot be read — answered as a declared unknown with zero sources, never a fabricated count
limitations: Semantic similarity discovers candidates; it does not prove behaviour, ownership or architecture, and the answer says so

Local word vectors are a 205-word programming vocabulary plus the project's own vocabulary hashed into 50 dimensions. Their cosines are not comparable with a model embedding's, and an identifier-shaped query whose tokens are all absent produces a zero vector, reported as `reason=degenerate-query-vector`
Coverage is per comparison space. On a mixed-model index the symbols comparable in the query model's space can be far fewer than the library-wide number; both numbers are reported and labelled

When the configured embedding provider does not answer within the tool's wait ceiling (2 s, or `BB_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_MS` when lower) the question is embedded with the local word-vector model, the answer declares the timeout, and the ranking is limited to that model's space

A verified aggregate is exact about the indexed snapshot, not the working tree: files changed after the last index write are not reflected, and the answer reports the snapshot time so the reader can judge the gap

The dense candidate scan is capped at `BB_VECTOR_SCAN_CAP` rows (default 20,000). When the cap is reached the answer declares `truncated=true`, and the candidates are a deterministic prefix of the embedding table ordered by entity id

A non-discriminative ranking (several candidates within the 0.05 margin of the best) publishes no numeric confidence: the answer says the scores do not separate candidates instead of printing a number it calls unreliable
tools.performance: Warm default-argument latency on the 3.6 GB reference index (6,452 files / 310,423 symbols) is p50 ≈ 1.8 s and p95 ≈ 2.1 s with the configured embedding provider; the first call in a cold process takes 9–10 s because the scan loads up to 20,000 vectors (≈164 MB at 2048 dimensions). The exact symbol-name route with `limit: 1` skips the dense scan and answers in milliseconds. The page size bounds both the payload and the work budget, and the candidate scan cap bounds memory independently of index size.
tools.safety: Read-only. Every index open is byte-read-only: the tool does not create a database, run migrations, heal indexes or promote embeddings, and it never writes source or rebuilds embeddings behind the caller's back. When embeddings are configured, the natural-language question itself is sent to that embedding provider to compute the query vector; with local word vectors the whole call stays offline.
tools.evidence: Treat matched symbols and resolvable source locations as evidence; treat similarity scores as candidate ranking, not proof. A non-discriminative ranking is not evidence and is labelled as such. A verified aggregate is a fact about the indexed snapshot, with that snapshot's timestamp reported.

tools.name: bb_health
tools.description: Unified index health: file/symbol/relationship/imports counts, embedding model + coverage, schema version, runtime, file freshness, what this call cost, and (when asked) the integrity battery, analysis-history totals and index completeness. There is no `mode` parameter: a call reports status, and `refresh`/`force` select the one behaviour that mutates the index. The default output names WHY each file was classified: `freshness why` separates fresh-verified-by-content-hash from fresh-verified-by-mtime+size-only (the file was not read), and names content-changed, deleted-from-disk, unreadable and unindexed separately, because those need different fixes and a single 'N stale' number is not actionable. Every report carries a top-level `healthy` boolean on the tool result (and inside the JSON payload when history=true): false exactly when the report contains an error-severity finding; a broken index is a successful REPORT, not a tool error (isError stays false), while wrong input is refused with isError. Options the chosen call cannot honour are refused: `limit` needs history=true; `wait` needs refresh/force; `sampleSize` belongs to sampled freshness only. Use verbose=true for a per-language breakdown, PER-LANGUAGE SEARCHABILITY (the share of each language's symbols a semantic query can reach — a language at 0% is invisible to bb_ask), the embedded/unembedded symbol kinds and stale-file names; verbose=true is also the only call that runs the per-symbol embedding aggregates, so a default call is bounded by the file count, not the symbol count. integrity=true runs the index integrity check battery, which NAMES each non-ok check with its remediation; with the default sampled freshness the battery falls back to a COMPLETE disk pass over the indexed files (it content-hashes files whose metadata changed), so it is materially more expensive than a status call. freshness="complete" (not a `complete` option) checks every indexed file instead of a sample; includeAnalysisRuns=true adds persisted run/finding totals; history=true answers with a JSON object { health, history, healthy } instead of the text report and is the only caller of `limit` (minimum 1, default 20). checkUnindexed=true walks the project and reports files the indexer would index but the index does not contain — a stat per eligible file, opt-in because a default call must not silently acquire a walk. refresh=true reindexes before reporting (`wait` defaults true; wait=false detaches it and the NEXT call reports the outcome once, success or failure); force=true wipes and rebuilds first and is DESTRUCTIVE. Freshness defaults to a DETERMINISTIC sample spread across the whole index: `stale` is then a lower bound on the project, not a total, and the report says so — pass freshness="complete" when you need the exact count.

verbose.description: include the per-language breakdown, per-language searchability, embedded/unembedded symbol kinds, embedding config/chain and stale/missing file names (default false). This is the only value that runs the per-symbol embedding aggregates; a default call skips them so it stays bounded by the file count

history.description: return persisted analysis history (default false). CHANGES THE OUTPUT SHAPE: this mode answers with a JSON object { health, history, healthy } instead of the text report, so a caller must not parse the text form when asking for it; the result also carries the same top-level `healthy` boolean as the text form

limit.description: analysis-history page size (default 20); must be a whole number >= 1 and is only read when history=true — supplying it without history is REFUSED

force.description: force a full in-place reindex before reporting — DESTRUCTIVE: the index is wiped before it is rebuilt, so a failure leaves it empty

wait.description: applies to refresh/force only (default true; supplying it without refresh/force is REFUSED). wait=false detaches the rebuild and returns the current snapshot; the NEXT call reports the detached outcome once — completion as well as failure

freshness.description: freshness mode (default sampled — a deterministic, unbiased sample spread over every indexed file, NOT the first N; freshness="complete" checks every indexed file and makes the stale count exact)

sampleSize.description: freshness sample count (default 200); must be a whole number >= 1 and applies to freshness="sampled" only — supplying it together with freshness="complete" is REFUSED

integrity.description: run the index integrity check battery (14 checks, each named with its remediation when not ok). Cost: with the default sampled freshness the battery performs a COMPLETE disk pass over the indexed files (content-hashing those whose metadata changed), so this is the most expensive opt-in

includeAnalysisRuns.description: add persisted analysis run/finding totals (full-table counts, not a page length)

paths.description: report the state of these project-relative files INSTEAD of a project-wide freshness answer — for the question an agent actually has after an edit, at O(files named) rather than O(project). At most 50, no duplicates, no blank entries. The answer is a SEPARATE self-describing block, so every other number in the report stays project-wide and the two can never be read as one. Each path is FIVE-state, not a boolean: fresh (indexed, on disk, unchanged), stale (content changed), gone (indexed, no longer readable on disk — `reason` distinguishes file-gone from unreadable), NOT-INDEXED (on disk, the indexer has not run since it appeared — a freshness verdict here would be meaningless), or absent (no such path). Paths that resolve outside the project, or through a symlink out of it, are REFUSED and reported as unchecked rather than answered

checkUnindexed.description: WALK the project and report files on disk that the indexer would index but the index does NOT contain — the direction freshness cannot see (freshness reports files IN the index and gone from disk). Costs a stat per eligible file, i.e. the discovery phase of an index run, so it is opt-in. Uses the INDEXER'S OWN discovery rules, so gitignored files, node_modules, unsupported extensions and >5MB files are correctly NOT counted, and the output names that population. Without this option, index completeness is not asserted at all

documentation.summary: Unified index, schema, freshness, embeddings, runtime, integrity, completeness and analysis-history report — status by default, one explicit refresh behaviour, and no `mode` parameter.

returns: Counts (files, symbols, relationships, imports, syntax-error files), schema version, runtime, embedding model/coverage and a `freshness` block that states whether it checked a SAMPLE or the whole index
The freshness reason mix per file (content-changed, deleted, unreadable, unindexed) and, on verbose, the bounded stale/missing file names
When `paths` is given: a separate five-state block (fresh / stale / gone / not-indexed / absent) for exactly those files, while every other number stays project-wide
When `checkUnindexed` is given: files on disk the indexer would index but the index does not contain, with the population named
When `integrity` is given: the integrity checks with their status and remediation, naming each non-ok check rather than only a score
When `includeAnalysisRuns` is given: persisted run/finding totals as full-table counts; `history` instead answers with JSON `{ health, history, healthy }`
A `healthy` boolean on the result (and inside the history JSON): false exactly when the report contains an error-severity finding
errors: An option the selected behaviour cannot honour: `limit` without `history=true`, `wait` without `refresh`/`force`, `sampleSize` with `freshness="complete"` — each refused with the accepted form named
Invalid values: unknown `freshness`, `sampleSize` below 1, a non-integer `limit` (and `limit: 0` with `history=true`)
`paths` problems: an empty list, more than 50 entries, duplicate entries, blank entries, or a path that escapes the project (directly or through a symlink)
An index that cannot be opened read-only is reported as an EMPTY_INDEX error finding, not as a tool failure: a broken index is a successful report
limitations: Sampled freshness (the default) is a deterministic sample, so `stale` is a LOWER BOUND on the project, not a total; `freshness="complete"` is the exact census
A `fresh` verdict reached through the mtime+size fast path never read the file: a same-size edit that preserves the mtime reads fresh (the same trade-off as git's stat-cache)
Embedding coverage reports stored vectors, not semantic quality or retrieval accuracy; verbose=true is what joins it to per-language searchability

`integrity: true` with the default sampled freshness performs a COMPLETE disk pass over the indexed files, and `checkUnindexed: true` walks the project — both are opt-in precisely because a default call must not acquire them

The default call does not run the per-symbol embedding aggregates (per-language symbol counts, searchable-by-language, embedded/unembedded kinds, provider chain); those run only for verbose=true, which is what keeps a default answer bounded by file count rather than symbol count
No `mode` parameter exists: a call reports status, and `refresh`/`force` are the only behaviours selected by flags
tools.performance: Measured warm through the MCP door on the campaign checkout: a default call answers in about 0.8 s p50 / 0.9 s p95 on the workspace index (6,452 files / 310,423 symbols / 3.6 GB), and about 2.6 s p50 / 3.3 s p95 on a 1,283,638-symbol copy of that index; the first call after a cold start measured 8.3 s and 25.3 s respectively on those two indexes. The 5-file polyglot fixture measures ~53 ms p50 and the 100-file synthetic fixture ~35 ms p50 through the same code path. `verbose=true` adds the per-symbol embedding aggregates, `integrity=true` adds a complete disk pass, `freshness="complete"` hashes/indexes every file, and `checkUnindexed=true` adds a project walk — all opt-in and declared for that reason.
tools.safety: A status call is read-only: the index is opened through the driver's read-only mode, so no migrations, healers or WAL writes run. refresh=true and force=true are the only index mutations and are explicit: refresh reindexes, force WIPES the index before rebuilding and is destructive; wait=false detaches a rebuild and the next call reports its outcome once. `healthy:false` never means the tool failed — the report is the answer.
tools.evidence: Counts, schema version and embedding rows are measured from the brain database; freshness compares indexed metadata with the filesystem and names the reason per file, separating content-verified fresh verdicts from mtime+size fast-path ones; integrity results are computed from stored rows and disk state; sampled answers declare that they are samples. `brain_index_status` counters are labelled when they describe the last index RUN rather than the index itself.

tools.name: bb_patterns
tools.description: Detect orphaned code, framework patterns, and anti-patterns, ranked by confidence, with staleness markers when a finding's file changed after indexing. Use scope=orphaned for dead code; scope=all (default) for the full pattern scan with the optional class/confidence filters. Orphan confidence is derived from evidence (0.30-0.70); anti-pattern confidence is 0.60-0.90; framework findings carry a fixed 0.6. `limit` is one bounded page (maximum 500) and the answer names the full census. Architecture and code-quality analysis are planned, not yet executable.

scope.description: orphaned only, or all pattern classes (default all)

limit.description: maximum findings displayed (default 20, maximum 500); the answer's census line reports the full count

includeOrphaned.description: include orphaned-code patterns in an all scan (default true)

confidenceThreshold.description: drop findings below this confidence (default 0 = report everything, ranked). Orphan confidence is evidence-derived and spans 0.30-0.70; anti-pattern confidence spans 0.60-0.90; framework findings are a fixed 0.6

history.description: return persisted pattern history (runs bounded by limit; the findings window and its total are declared in the answer)

recordRun.description: persist this scan as an analysis run (persists the whole census, not the displayed page; works in both scopes; capped at 50,000 findings with the cap disclosed)

documentation.summary: Pattern/orphan analysis ranked by confidence, with a bounded page, a declared census, per-finding staleness, and optional persisted run history.

returns: A bounded page of findings (default 20, maximum 500): rule/type, file:line, symbol for orphan rules, confidence, and a per-finding [stale] marker when the finding's file changed after indexing
A census line naming the full finding count and the per-rule breakdown, so the page never reads as the population
scope=orphaned: suppression accounting (every candidate the scan discarded, by reason), refused-usage counts (selfLoop/inferred/lowConfidence), and import-resolution counts
provenance line: evidence class, engine, symbols/files scanned, limitations count
Explicit JSON when history=true: runs bounded by limit, a findings window (200) with findingsTotal/findingsReturned/findingsTruncated declared
errors: scope must be one of: orphaned, all
confidenceThreshold must be between 0 and 1
limit must be a whole number >= 0; above 500 it is refused by name (the census line reports the full count)
unknown or irrelevant options are refused and the accepted options are named
No index found for <project>: run: bb index <project> — an unindexed project is a named refusal, never a clean zero
limitations: A finding is not a deletion instruction. The tool reports what the index does and does not record; where the index is silent, the finding says so on its face rather than presenting absence of evidence as evidence of absence.

The text answer does not include the engine's per-finding evidence array, limitations array or remediation text. Those travel on the engine report (PatternFinding) that the text is rendered from; the answer surface carries the aggregate disclosures listed under Returns.

Confidence is derived from evidence classes, not assigned per rule. Orphans span 0.30-0.70 (0.30-0.55 for file findings); anti-patterns span 0.60-0.90. Name-unique orphan candidates measured a 0.0% false-positive rate against a source-text oracle; ambiguous names measured 14.4%; per-corpus rates are a lower bound because the oracle cannot see reflection or template indirection.
Framework findings carry a FIXED confidence of 0.6 — that is the whole population of that rule, so a threshold above 0.6 removes every framework finding at once rather than discriminating among them.

A relationship counts as usage evidence only when it is not a self-loop, its published evidenceClass is not "inferred", and its confidence is at least 0.7. Refused rows are counted in the orphaned answer's [usage-evidence] line and itemised on the findings they would have cleared.

A finding whose symbol had no recorded incoming reference while its file did carries a coverage-gap indicator: that is the signature of an analyzer that reached the file and not the declaration, and such a finding may be a coverage gap rather than dead code.

Dynamic dispatch, reflection and string-keyed lookups are invisible to the index; the engine never fabricates a resolved edge for them, so a symbol reached only that way is reported with the limitation stated on the finding.

Lifecycle methods can look unreferenced because a framework invokes them by convention rather than by a recorded call: Ruby "initialize", constructors in Java/Kotlin/C#/Python, and similar framework entry points are known false-positive classes. Treat them as entry points when reviewing a report.

Test files are excluded from candidates but not from evidence: a production symbol called only from a test is not reported, and a production file imported only by a test is not reported as orphaned. The engine option includeTests (true means "also report test symbols") is an engine API option, not a bb_patterns parameter.

Framework and anti-pattern detection is heuristic and confidence-qualified; non-code languages (JSON, YAML, Markdown, ...) contribute no symbol candidates and no anti-pattern findings, though they are still indexed and checked as whole files.
tools.performance: A default call ({} — all scope, limit 20) measured on the reference index (6,452 files / 310,423 symbols / 820,040 relationships) at T2: TODO-MEASURE. The cost is index-bound and grows with the SYMBOL count, not the relationship count: every usage set the scan builds is reduced in SQL and bounded by the symbol count. The tool opens the database byte-read only, so a read does not pay the write path's migration/healer cost. limit bounds the displayed page only; the census in the header is the full candidate count, and `raise `limit`` is shown when the page is short.
tools.safety: The read path is byte-read-only: db and WAL are unchanged by a call (the -shm read marks may move). A read never creates an index or a schema. recordRun is the one write and it is opt-in: it persists analysis-history records (never source), records the whole census up to a declared 50,000-finding cap rather than the displayed page, and reports the recorded count and any cap on the answer.
tools.evidence: The wire answer is deliberately explicit about its own coverage: census and per-rule counts, suppression accounting by reason (orphaned scope), refused usage rows by reason and import-resolution counts (orphaned scope), provenance (evidence class, engine, symbols/files scanned), and per-finding staleness markers with a manual-repair footer. The engine report beneath it additionally carries a per-finding evidence array, limitations array and remediation text; those are engine-report fields, available through the library API rather than the MCP text surface.

tools.name: bb_security
tools.description: Taint-flow security scan over the indexed source-to-sink flows: SQL injection, XSS, command injection, path traversal, insecure deserialization, SSRF, open redirect and code execution. Flows whose endpoints both resolve to indexed symbols are findings; one-sided flows are reported separately as unvalidated observations, never as confirmed exploits. Reads are read-only against the index; an unindexed project is refused by name. Findings whose underlying file changed after indexing carry a staleness marker.

recordRun.description: persist this scan as an analysis run

documentation.summary: Taint-flow findings over the index, with optional persisted run history. A flow is a finding only when both endpoints resolve to indexed symbols; one-sided flows are reported as unvalidated observations. A findings answer states the pre-cap census so a capped scan is never mistaken for a complete one; a history answer states its run count and its finding total, and its findings page is capped and declared. Reads open the index read-only and refuse an unindexed project; recordRun is the one write. Not detected: hardcoded secrets; genuine cross-language taint; standalone weak crypto.

returns: A findings answer: one line per finding with severity, label, symbol, resolved `file:line`, source and sink type, and `[mitigated]` / `[stale]` flags when they apply — at most 20 findings are rendered per answer

A `[scan: …]` census line stating how many taint flows were indexed, how many findings they deduplicated into, how many are shown, how many are beyond the scan cap, and — when the cap bites — the explicit `CAPPED at <cap>` sentence naming how many findings were not examined
One-sided flows listed separately as unvalidated observations, each with its real severity, its location and the reason it is unvalidated (at most 5 rendered; the census names the total)
A staleness footer only when a finding's file changed after indexing: `N stale, M missing of K finding file(s)` plus the manual repair command; silence when everything is fresh

A history answer: a JSON page with the persisted runs (bounded by `limit`), the persisted findings (capped at 200 with `findingsTotal`/`findingsShown`/`findingsTruncated`), the finding-state summary, and a `census` object. Persisted findings carry the engine's evidence, calibrated confidence and per-finding limitations; unvalidated observations are never persisted
errors: Unavailable index — every door (MCP, CLI, library) refuses by name; a read never creates an index
Invalid history limit (non-integer, or negative)
Unknown option (rejected with the accepted set named)
`limit` without `history: true` (refused: it would be accepted and then ignored)
`history` together with `recordRun` (refused: they are different answers; pass one)
limitations: Static taint analysis can produce false positives and false negatives
It is not runtime testing or a penetration test

`confirmed` means both flow endpoints are indexed symbols — it does **not** prove the values are connected. The indexer pairs every taint source with every taint sink in a symbol body, so two tokens in one function produce a confirmed flow whether or not one reaches the other

**Not detected:** hardcoded secrets (no such finding type is emitted; that rule belongs to `bb_patterns`), genuine cross-*language* taint (the `crossLanguage` flag means the flow was stitched across symbols, not that languages differ), standalone weak-crypto use (emitted as a sink with no co-located source, so it remains an observation)

Severity is normalized into exactly `critical|high|medium|low|unknown`; an unrecognised stored value becomes `unknown` rather than vanishing from the counts. Persisted history stores the normalized grade of a confirmed/mitigated flow, so an ungradeable resolved flow is recorded as `unknown`

A parameterized or escaped sink may still be reported: the indexer matcher is token-based and does not track sanitizers, so validate a critical finding against the actual data flow before acting on it
tools.performance: A findings answer is bounded by the engine's scan cap (500 flows) and renders at most 20 findings plus 5 observations; the census line states when the cap dropped findings. `recordRun` re-scans with a census-sized cap (50,000) so the persisted snapshot is the analysed set rather than the display window, and the same CAPPED sentence appears if even that cap bites. A history answer is bounded by `limit` on runs and by a 200-finding page with the true total declared. Reads open the index read-only and never reindex a file.
tools.safety: Reads are read-only: the index is opened with the driver's read-only mode, so a read runs no migrations and moves no WAL. `recordRun` is the one write — it stores analysis-history rows — and, because it opens the database for writing, it may also run the additive open-path migrations every write path runs. No source file is ever modified.
tools.evidence: A finding is supported by indexed source/sink locations and relationship paths; severity does not imply exploitability. The text answer renders the finding's location, source and sink type; the calibrated confidence (0.7 confirmed / 0.4 observation / 0.3 mitigated) and the taint-flow evidence are carried in the history JSON, which is the persisted evidence. Unvalidated observations are never persisted to history.

tools.name: bb_visualize
tools.description: Scoped dependency and architecture visualization: one bounded projection over the index's stored symbol and relationship rows, with explicit filters, provenance, truncation, machine-readable JSON, and genuinely self-contained HTML (no network, no fonts, no build step — it renders offline, in an air-gapped editor, anywhere). The answer is an AUDITABLE projection of the index, not a picture: every link carries the stored relationship row it traces to (rowId) and its stored confidence, and every node carries its line, lineEnd and qualifiedName, so the graph is navigable and every edge can be checked against the row that justifies it. Distinct relationship types between the same pair are SEPARATE links, so a pair that is both contains and exports renders as both. Node size follows the index’s own gravity score. In the HTML, edge opacity encodes stored confidence, relationship type sets colour and a structural/behavioural dash, a CROSS-LANGUAGE edge gets its own wide dash and is drawn beneath the local edges so a polyglot project shows where one language hands off to another, and a stale endpoint (file changed since index) is drawn as a hollow ring; links inherit worst-of-endpoints. Nodes are grouped into the NAMED REGION they live in — a directory of the project, a directory with fewer than three matching symbols folded into its parent — each region placed at its own anchor inside a rounded pod and switchable from the sidebar like any other class, At overview zoom an edge BETWEEN two regions is drawn as one REGION LINK per region pair — dotted, because it is a summary and not a stored row; its width and alpha come from how many stored edges it stands for — while an edge INSIDE one region is always drawn as itself, and the individual cross-region edges return past ~1.15x zoom or when a link is opened (double-click frames both of its regions). Edges drawn individually are capped at a zoom-dependent count with the readout naming the cap, because an uncapped aggregate is a smear rather than a map; the frame's readout reconciles the picture with the census (how many cross-region edges the links stand for, how many pairs exist, how to open them), the sidebar's live line repeats it, and the links — with their regions, counts, stored rows, commonest relationship and screen geometry — are PUBLISHED on the view's API rather than only painted, because a summary that can only be seen cannot be checked. Moving the pointer across the map never changes the view: hover emphasises the node's own edges, and a CLICK is what focuses, so the map cannot dissolve under the reader's hand. The graph has TWO arrangements and the reader picks: `layout: "regions"` (the default) is the region map described above, and `layout: "force"` drops the directories entirely — one force layout, no region pods and no region links, every stored edge drawn as itself under the same zoom-dependent cap — which is the graph as it looked before the regions existed, and which is the honest shape for a project whose parts do not fall along directory lines. The layout is written onto the document itself (data-bb-layout) and both arrangements are offered as a switch in the generated page's sidebar, so `layout` sets the arrangement the page OPENS with and the reader can move between them without regenerating anything. The picked-item panel is deliberately not a modal: it docks to either side of the frame and collapses to its own heading — which always names what is picked — while KEEPING the selection, because hiding a panel to see the picture must not cost the reader the focus and the zoom they just asked for (its X is the control that clears). The layout runs in frame-sized slices with a progress readout, so the artifact stays interactive and visible at the maximum graph size and in a background tab. Every answer declares its bounds as three DISTINCT numbers — totalNodesAvailable (what the scope and filters actually match), truncation.originalNodes (what reached the projection) and nodes (what was returned) — and the HTML artifact carries the same declaration in its machine-readable payload (`declared`), so a short page can never be mistaken for a whole set in any format. `offset` walks that same order rather than re-reading the first page: the ranking carries a final `s.id` tiebreaker so page k+1 begins exactly where page k ended, and `considered.page` declares which page the answer is, of how many, and where the next one starts (null on the last) — a scope larger than one page can be walked, and an offset past the end is stated as an empty PAGE rather than as an empty project. Whatever the noise filter removes is counted onto excluded with the patterns responsible — always present, including when it is empty, so silence and zero are never confused — and an empty answer is declaredAbsent with a reason rather than an empty result that looks like a real project. `considered` declares what the answer actually READ: how many relationships exist, how many the query read, and in what words the selection is an arbitrary primary-key slice rather than a ranking, plus which symbols got a chance to be in the graph and in what order. `considered.overlays` carries the index's OTHER facts about the returned symbols — agent annotations from `bb_annotate`, matched by NAME AND PATH (never by name alone: two symbols can share a name, and a note is about one of them), with the notes themselves, the author class, and a count of notes that name a symbol of this scope at another path and are therefore NOT attached. The layer is declared even when it is empty, so "no agent has annotated these symbols" and "nobody looked" are different replies. Language filters are applied BEFORE the limit, so a rare language receives the same budget as a common one. The DEFAULT text format carries the same declared coverage, selection and exclusion as the JSON one, so the reply a caller gets without asking is the reply that can be audited. Member-level relationships are FOLDED onto the owner class, and every folded edge says so: when a class-like symbol is selected and a relationship is stored on one of its MEMBERS that is not itself in the node set, the row is attributed to the owner and the edge carries ownerCascade with matchedMembers naming the member it came through — so an attributed edge is never presented as one the index stored between the two drawn nodes. The fold is deliberately narrow (one level, class-like owners only, never for contains, an exact edge always preferred to an attributed one) and `considered.ownerCascade` declares whether it ran, how many members it scanned, how many rows it folded and whether a cap truncated it, so "nothing to fold" and "the fold never ran" are distinguishable. This is NOT bb_graph's depth-N traversal: the edge set is the relationships between the selected nodes, plus the folded member rows.

target.description: file, module, symbol, or feature target (`symbol` and `query` are accepted as aliases for `target`)

maxNodes.description: max nodes (default 200, accepted range 1-2000); 0 and anything above the ceiling are REFUSED with the range named rather than clamped, because a returned page must mean the page that was asked for

maxLinks.description: max links (default 5000, accepted range 1-20000); 0 and anything above the ceiling are REFUSED with the range named rather than clamped, because a returned page must mean the page that was asked for

offset.description: how many symbols of the ranking to SKIP before this page starts (default 0; a whole number >= 0, refused rather than normalised). The order is the scope's own ranking with a final `s.id` tiebreaker, so page k+1 begins where page k ended and no symbol is repeated or lost. `considered.page` states the page number, the page count, the total matching the scope, and the next offset (null on the last page). Without this, a scope bigger than `maxNodes` had symbols that could not be asked for at all

relationshipTypes.description: relationship type filter. Matched case-insensitively against the index's OWN stored spellings, and a type the index does not contain is REJECTED with the stored set named (never answered as zero links, which would read like a project with no calls). The applied filter is echoed in considered.relationshipTypesConsidered.

symbolKinds.description: symbol kinds to KEEP (class, interface, struct, enum, function, method, property, constant, variable, ...). Omitted = every kind, and on a real project gravity ranks files’ constants and properties first: the reply states the composition it returned in `considered.kindCensus`, so a graph of string constants is visible as one rather than mistaken for the architecture. Matched case-insensitively against the index’s own spellings, and a kind the index does not contain is REJECTED with the stored set named (never answered as zero nodes). The applied filter is echoed in considered.symbolKindsConsidered.

languages.description: language filter. Matched case-insensitively against the index's OWN stored spellings, and an unknown language is REJECTED with the stored set named (never answered as zero nodes). Applied BEFORE the node limit, so a rare language receives the same budget as a common one, and the applied filter is echoed in considered.languagesConsidered.

excludePatterns.description: path SEGMENTS treated as build noise and excluded. Matched on whole segments, never as substrings — a substring rule removed `src/util/edit_distance.rs` because `dist` is inside `edit_distance`, and `src/compiler/layout.rs` because `out` is inside `layout`. Omit to use the defaults (node_modules, .git, .next, .turbo, .cache, coverage, dist, build, out, target, vendor, __pycache__)

includeTests.description: include test/spec sources. Default true: they are ordinary source. When false, test/spec/testdata directories and *_test.* / *spec.* files are excluded and counted

view.description: The dependency map (nodes are symbols, lines are relationships, sized by stored evidence). Accepts only `graph`; any other value is REFUSED rather than answered as the graph.

layout.description: the GRAPH view's arrangement, and the only option here that shapes the picture without changing the data. `regions` (default) groups every node into the DIRECTORY it lives in, anchors and names each region, and summarises the edges between regions as one dotted region link per pair at the overview. `force` ignores directories entirely: one force layout, no pods and no region links, every stored edge drawn as itself under a zoom-dependent cap the readout names. The generated page carries BOTH as a switch in its sidebar, so this sets the arrangement the page OPENS with; the layout is declared on the document itself (data-bb-layout), so the file draws what it says it is.

documentation.summary: Scoped canonical dependency graphs with explicit truncation and provenance.

returns: Canonical nodes and links, with EVERY stored relationship type between a pair kept as a separate link

An auditable projection rather than a picture: each link carries `rowId` (the stored relationship it traces to), its stored `confidence` and its line, and `crossLanguage` where the edge crosses a language boundary; each node carries `line`, `lineEnd` and `qualifiedName`, so the graph is navigable and every edge can be checked against the row that justifies it

Three DISTINCT declared counts — `totalNodesAvailable` (what the scope and filters match), `truncation.originalNodes` (what reached the projection) and `nodes` (what was returned) — so a short page is never mistaken for a whole set

`considered` — what the answer actually READ: how many relationships exist, how many the query read, and in what words the selection is an arbitrary primary-key slice rather than a ranking, plus which symbols got a chance to be in the graph and in what order
`excluded` — what the noise filter removed, how many, and the patterns responsible — always present, including when it is empty, so silence and zero are never confused
`declaredAbsent` with an `absenceNote` when the answer is empty, distinguishing what matched nothing from what matched but did not survive the projection

Text, JSON, or genuinely SELF-CONTAINED HTML: one file with no network, no fonts and no build step, carrying its own force-directed layout and canvas renderer, so it renders offline and in an air-gapped editor

In the HTML the evidence is ENCODED rather than decorated: edge opacity is stored confidence, relationship type sets colour and a structural/behavioural dash, a cross-language edge gets its own wide dash and is drawn beneath the local edges, a stale endpoint is a hollow ring, node size is the index's own gravity, and any node or edge can be selected to read its stored facts
The DEFAULT text format carries the same declared coverage, selection and exclusion as the JSON one, so the reply a caller gets without asking is the reply that can be audited

`view` is `graph` and rides the result as `view`: the force-directed dependency map (nodes are symbols, lines are relationships, sized by stored evidence). Any other value is refused rather than answered as the graph.
errors: Missing target for a scoped graph
Unsupported scope or format
Unavailable index
limitations: The graph reflects static indexed relationships

THE EDGE SET IS COMPLETE for the returned nodes, not a slice of the relationship table. It used to be neither fast nor right: the query read `LIMIT maxLinks*3` rows in PRIMARY KEY order and found ZERO of the 1,142 relationships that actually connect 400 selected symbols, because the slice is uncorrelated with the node set. Edges are now fetched by joining both endpoints, so the answer states a complete fact and no M-of-N apology is needed

THE NODE SET IS A SELECTION, and says so. Project and feature scope take the index's own gravity, so the graph is the busiest core rather than a sample; file, module and symbol scope take source order, because that is the only order a reader of one file would want. `considered.nodeSelection` names which applied

A MERGED EDGE KEEPS ITS WEIGHT. Several stored relationship rows share one (source, target, type) — a call made from 15 call sites is one drawn edge but 15 pieces of evidence. MEASURED on cargo: 394 stored rows between 200 returned nodes collapse to 285 links, so 109 rows used to vanish with nothing to say so. The graph shape is right to merge them, since 15 parallel edges would be noise; the weight is what distinguishes a hot edge from a stray reference, so `occurrences` and every `rowId` ride the edge, thickness encodes it, and the readout totals the stored rows behind the drawn edges

PERFORMANCE IS BOUNDED BY THE OUTPUT BUDGET, and the largest budget is the slowest case. Measured on cargo at the documented maximum of maxNodes 2000: the edge query binds two placeholders per symbol, so 4,000 symbols bind 8,000 parameters — 12.5 ms at 200 nodes, 322 ms at 1,000, 1,340 ms at 4,000. A temp-table formulation of the same join was measured and is WORSE (2,574 ms), because SQLite plans `IN (SELECT ...)` as a repeated index seek, so the direct bind is kept and the cost is declared rather than hidden. `brain_symbol(project_id, gravity_score DESC, line_start)` removes a 40,595-row sort from every call and is created on open, not only on fresh databases

NOISE FILTER (declared, and the caller's to change). Build output and VCS metadata are excluded by default, matched on whole path SEGMENTS. This was previously a bare-substring rule that removed real source: measured on cargo, `dist` removed `src/util/edit_distance.rs`, `out` removed `src/compiler/layout.rs` and `src/compiler/output_depinfo.rs`, and `build` removed `crates/cargo-test-support/build.rs`, leaving 225 of 1,787 symbol-bearing files with no exclusion declared anywhere. Test and spec sources are ordinary source and are INCLUDED by default; `excludePatterns` and `includeTests` change all of it, and whatever is removed is counted onto `excluded`

SCOPE TARGETS ARE VALUES, not patterns. `%` and `_` match themselves and a directory prefix matches on a segment boundary, so `src/util` never reaches `src/utilities`. This matches bb_analyze, whose contract states the same rule; the two tools previously disagreed, and this one was the permissive one (measured: a target of `%` selected every file in the corpus)

LANGUAGE FILTERS ARE APPLIED BEFORE THE LIMIT, not after it. They used to be applied in memory to an already-truncated selection ordered by gravity, so a language whose symbols were not in that slice was cut before the filter ran: measured on cargo, `languages: ['javascript']` returned 0 nodes and declared the project had none, while the index held 56 javascript symbols — and the declared total counted the language in SQL while the returned nodes did not, so one reply contradicted itself. `relationshipTypes` deliberately filters edges rather than nodes, and says so: a caller narrowing edges must not change which nodes exist

`feature` scope matches a symbol NAME or a docstring. The docstring half is thin in practice and the answer does not pretend otherwise: measured on cargo, 70 of 40,595 symbols (0.17%) carry one, so a feature query is usually a name match
Nodes and links beyond configured budgets are omitted and reported

THE DOCUMENT SAVES ITSELF. Reported more than once, and the gap is real: the artifact arrives as a blob of text and a reader who wants to keep it has no way to. Each document re-serialises its own live page through a Blob and an object URL -- not a data: URI, which several browsers reject at the 300KB-7MB these documents routinely reach -- and publishes that as `saveHtml`, because the control for it belongs in the viewer's Download section rather than floating over the drawing
tools.performance: maxNodes, maxLinks, scope, relationshipTypes, and languages constrain graph construction.
tools.safety: Read-only. HTML output contains the same bounded graph as JSON and does not mutate the project.
tools.evidence: Nodes and links resolve to canonical indexed entities; links with omitted endpoints are not emitted.

tools.name: bb_migrate
tools.description: Read-only single or batch migration planning with dependency order, explicit effort methodology, library mappings, risks, truncation, and unsupported cases. Plans whose source file changed since the last index are flagged stale up front — a plan is a claim about current code; JSON output carries the freshness block.

symbolNames.description: one or more symbols to migrate

paths.description: project-relative file or DIRECTORY paths; every indexed symbol in them joins the request, so a whole module can be planned in one call. UNION with symbolNames, not a replacement: naming a symbol AND a path that contains it plans it once

symbolIds.description: indexed symbol ids, the ONLY unambiguous way to name a component. Use this when a refusal reported that a name matches several symbols; a name is not an identity, and two components can share one name in two files

documentation.summary: Batch cross-language migration plans with ordering, waves, cohort rollup, scope completeness, and unsupported mappings.

returns: Dependency-ordered migration plans, grouped into parallel-workable waves
Scope completeness: how much of the cited integration surface the request actually covers
Cohort rollup by source file and by wave
Effort methodology, library mappings, and risks
Explicit unsupported and truncation results, naming the symbols the cap dropped
errors: Missing targetLanguage
No symbolName, symbolNames or paths
A path that matches no indexed file (the tool says so rather than returning an empty plan set)
Unknown option
limitations: Plans are estimates, not translated source
Library mappings are advisory and unsupported routes remain explicit

Dependency ordering and mapping depend on the analyzer-extracted symbol and relationship graph; edge cases that the analyzers cannot resolve (reflection, dynamic dispatch, or cross-file relations the grammar does not model) limit the completeness of the resulting plan

Library dependencies are read from the index's per-file import rows and split into standard library, third-party, local and unclassified; a third-party library with no registered mapping is named at confidence 0 and charged 6h of research, never claimed as supported

A request names a bounded set of symbols, and the cited integration surface is usually much larger: measured 98.6-99.8% out of scope on cobra for requests of 1-16 symbols. The `scope` block reports this on every result

56 of 486 dictionary rows (11.5%) are not import specifiers — API idioms, a framework, Flutter widget class names, display names with a space, and a mis-keyed dart->typescript block — so they cannot be reached by an import lookup. Audited by script/m20/verify-migration-dictionary.ts
tools.performance: Work is bounded by the requested symbols' own fan-in and fan-out, not by repository size. A request is capped at 100 symbols; the dropped names are reported in `truncation.cappedNames`.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not generate, replace, or compile target-language source.
tools.evidence: Dependency ordering comes from indexed relationships; effort and mappings are labeled methodology-driven estimates. Relationship line, confidence, cross-language flag and bridge mechanism are read from the index; none is synthesized.

tools.name: bb_analyze
tools.description: Unified evidence-backed analysis over graph relationships, dependencies, project statistics, complexity, impact, and test intelligence. Select exactly one mode. Every read mode carries a freshness block (fresh/stale/missing counts + remediation) resolved against the live working tree, and report rows carry a stale flag when their file changed after indexing. Every mode is BOUNDED and says so: `limit` is the most items returned (edges per direction for callers/callees/trace, files for dependencies, entries for the test modes, the same everywhere) and the answer reports what it returned against what exists, so a page is never read as the whole set. callers/callees/trace/impact share the graph engine's owner-cascade semantics — a relationship stored against a class member is attributed to the owner class — and every edge states which it was through `targetMatch`. WHICH symbol the name resolved to is declared as well: `rootMatch` is `exact`, `exact-any-kind` or `containment`, and `containment` means the answer is about a symbol whose name CONTAINS the one asked for, or differs only in case — `found: true` on its own does not mean the name was itself a symbol. Locations are project-relative. Per-mode parameters: target applies to callers, callees, trace, complexity, impact, and test_impact; filePath scopes dependencies, test_mapping, test_gaps, and test_quality to a project-relative path PREFIX and is REFUSED (not ignored) on every other mode; limit applies to callers, callees, trace, dependencies, test_mapping, test_gaps and test_quality and is refused elsewhere; stats is always project-wide.

target.description: A symbol name for callers/callees/trace/impact/test_impact, or a project-relative FILE PATH for complexity (an exact file, or a directory prefix at any depth INCLUDING a top-level one; anything else is refused rather than treated as a path fragment). `symbol`/`symbolName`/`query` are accepted as aliases. A target is a VALUE, never a pattern: `%`, `_` and `\` are escaped and match themselves. Echoed back bounded at 200 characters with its full length stated — the search always uses the whole string.

filePath.description: Project-relative path PREFIX scoping dependencies, test_mapping, test_gaps and test_quality. Refused on every other mode. Matched on a whole segment boundary, so `src/util` does not match `src/utilities`.

limit.description: Maximum items returned: edges per direction for callers/callees/trace, files for dependencies, entries for test_mapping/test_gaps/test_quality. Defaults: 25 edges per direction, 20 files, 50 entries. Range 1-5000 (graph modes) or 1-2000 (the rest); 0 and anything above the ceiling are REFUSED rather than clamped, because a returned page must mean the page that was asked for. The answer reports what it returned and whether that is the whole set. Refused on the modes it does not apply to.

documentation.summary: One typed analysis surface over the graph, the file graph, project counts, complexity, impact and test evidence. Every mode is bounded, declares its own bounds, and reports what it returned against what exists.

defaults.limit: 25 edges per direction (callers/callees/trace); 20 files (dependencies); 50 entries (test_mapping/test_gaps); 50 files (test_quality)
defaults.target: required for callers, callees, trace, impact, test_impact; optional file path or directory prefix for complexity
defaults.filePath: optional path prefix (or an exact file) for dependencies, test_mapping, test_gaps, test_quality

returns: Mode-specific typed analysis: graph edges, file dependency edges, project counts, complexity metrics, impact, or test evidence
A declared bound on every answer — what was returned, what exists, and whether the set is the whole one
Explicit unavailable states: a metric or target that cannot be computed is `available: false` / `notFoundReason`, never a substituted number
errors: Missing required mode
Missing or blank target for a target-based mode
Option irrelevant to the selected mode (refused, never ignored)
`limit` on a mode it does not apply to, or `limit: 0`
A `complexity` target that names no indexed file and no directory prefix
limitations: Static relationships cannot establish runtime behavior
Test results describe indexed static evidence, not executed coverage; a project whose tests the indexer did not recognise is reported as having none, with the reason

Callers/callees/trace/impact modes share the graph engine's owner-cascade semantics: a relationship stored against a class member is attributed to the owner class. Every edge states which it was through `targetMatch` (`exact` or `owner-cascade`); absent means the engine could not tell, which is not the same as `exact`

Callers/callees/trace answer from the graph engine's DEFAULT kind set, which is EVERY kind the index stores — so a `callers` set means "who has a stored edge INTO this", not only who calls it. `contains` is the parent→member edge, so a class that CONTAINS a symbol is reported as that member's caller (membership, not dependency); `uses`/`references` are lexical evidence and `imports`/`exports` are module-level. Measured on this engine's own answers: lodash `baseConvert` answered 99 `calls` rows of 230 edges, cobra `getCompletions` 36 of 65, rake `standard_rake_options` 72 of 76. Every edge carries its stored `relationshipType`, so the composition is readable per answer. Mode `impact` does NOT share that set: it walks the declared dependency kinds (`calls`, `instantiates`, `extends`, `implements` — `src/lsp/impact.ts` `IMPACT_REL_TYPES`) and states the rule it applied, so a `callers` count and an `impact` count about the same symbol answer different questions

A name resolves to ONE stored symbol, and WHICH one is declared in `rootMatch`: `exact` (a structural symbol of that name), `exact-any-kind` (a symbol of that name the graph cannot traverse — a constant, a type alias — which still has callers), or `containment`. `containment` is the documented near-miss fallback and means the answer is about a symbol whose name CONTAINS the one asked for. Measured on this repository's src: `target: "us"` answered `found: true` rooted at `analyzeCSharpBareIdentifierUses`, and `target: "_"` answered `found: true` rooted at `build_registry` when no symbol is named `_`. `found: true` alone does not mean the name was a symbol

A CASE difference resolves by containment, because the exact step is `name = ?` (case-sensitive) and SQLite's `LIKE` is case-insensitive for ASCII. So `target: "HUB"` and `target: "hub"` are the same answer, reached by the weaker step — which is why `rootMatch` says `containment` for the first

`limit` has two ends and both are declared: refused below 1 (an empty page is indistinguishable from a real answer) and refused above 5,000 for the graph modes / 2,000 for the rest. It is refused rather than clamped, because a returned page must mean the page that was asked for. Measured on this repository's src, `limit: 2147483648` was accepted before this and answered with the whole corpus

`complexity` accepts a directory prefix at ANY depth, including a top-level directory. It did not: the prefix branch required a `/` in the target, so `target: "ast"` was refused as "no indexed file matches" while 84 indexed files sat under it, and the same for every top-level directory on every project

`complexity` publishes both file counts: `filesMatchingScope` is how many files the scope names and `filesInScope` is how many hold a symbol the metrics are over. They differ when a file in scope has no indexed symbol (83 of 84, measured), and `linesOfCode` covers the second number — so the gap is visible instead of an unexplained discrepancy

`test_mapping.summary.productionSymbols` and `test_gaps.summary.productionSymbols` are the SAME number, and each report also states `excludedAsNoise`, so `productionSymbols + excludedAsNoise` is the store's population under the mode's own filter. `test_gaps.summary.total` is a count of GAPS, not of production symbols — it is the population minus `directlyTested`, and the identity closes in public

A `not-found` answer is bounded: the target is echoed at most 200 characters with its full length stated. A 4,000-character target produced a 9,409-byte answer (~2.6k tokens for two words of information) before this. The bound is on the ECHO only — the search always uses the whole string
A name resolves among several stored symbols. `rootCandidates` says how many — 1 means the name was unique, more means the answer is about one of several

mode `impact` refuses a target the graph cannot root at, with `notFoundReason: "not-traversable"` and the symbol type. Measured on a fixture: a type alias and a namespace refuse; a constant and an enum DO root (`found: true`, `rootMatch: "exact-any-kind"`), so the kind alone does not predict the outcome — the field does. Such a symbol IS in the index; `callers`/`callees` resolve the same name because they match any type
A depth-capped walk is TRUNCATION and says so: `summary.truncated` is true with `truncationReason` naming the depth cap, beside `maxDepth` and `maxDepthReached`

`test_impact` refuses `limit`, so its declared bound is the same 2,000 ms walk ceiling the command accepts no page size for: `summary` carries `returned`, `total`, `truncated`, `truncationReason`, `timeBudgetMs`, `timeBudgetExhausted` and `depthCap`. An answer with `truncated: true` names the bound that fired

`test_quality`'s `limit` bounds the files ANALYSED and the files RETURNED: `summary` carries `returned`, `totalFiles` and `truncated`, so `limit: 1` answers one row and says it is one of three, not three rows with no page statement
`complexity`'s `breakdown` is a page of at most the 20 highest-complexity symbols; `breakdownReturned` and `breakdownTruncated` state what was cut, beside `symbolCount` (the population)

A record's `stale` flag means its file changed after indexing OR is gone from disk: `missing` is not `fresh`, and the modes that carry row flags (callers/callees/trace/dependencies/complexity/impact/test_mapping/test_gaps/test_quality) all mark it

`dependencies` and the three test modes accept an EXACT project-relative file as `filePath`, not only a directory prefix; matching is on a whole segment boundary, so `src/util` does not match `src/utilities`

These three modes' walks run under a wall-clock ceiling THIS TOOL declares — 2,000 ms, published on the answer as `summary.timeBudgetMs` with `summary.timeBudgetExhausted` saying whether it fired (`walk-time-budget-exhausted` among the reasons). It is not an inherited engine default: the graph engine applies no clock bound unless a caller asks for one, so the ceiling is visible here rather than implicit. It is kept because `mode=trace` on a hub is the walk that motivated a clock bound at all. A node is not a unit of work: the per-node caller query is priced by the reproducible ORDER BY, which SQLite applies before the LIMIT, so `edgeLimit` cannot bound it. Measured on this repository's own src: 2,436 matching rows for one symbol cost 85.8 ms of the 87.8 ms, and the walk was unbounded until this budget existed

`dependencies` resolves an internal specifier against the importing file's own directory and LABELS each edge `resolved` / `suffix-match` / `unresolved`. It is not a guess from a basename: on this repository's own src only 74 of 906 `imports` relationships carry both endpoints and `brain_import.resolved_symbol_id` is empty, so specifier resolution is the primary path, not a fallback
A file's `dependents` and `dependencies` lists are capped per row; `dependentsTotal` / `dependenciesTotal` are the real sizes and the Truncated flags say the list was cut

Neither list carries `fileId` — a file id is `<40-hex project id>:<relative path>`, so it repeated the path printed beside it (56,540 of 121,340 bytes on a default page of this repository's src). The path is the locator, `resolution` says how it was reached, and the row above carries the id for the file the row is about

`metrics.couplingEdges` counts only the relationship types listed in `couplingRelationshipTypes`; `exports` and `contains` are index bookkeeping. `stats.relationships` is every row and is a different number
`metrics.maintainability` is unavailable when the formula's domain does not cover the scope (it is negative above roughly 3·10⁴ non-blank lines) rather than clamped to 0
Locations are project-relative. `nodes[].filePath` (absolute) is not emitted, so the same question returns the same bytes on any machine
A mapping entry carries at most 20 links (`linksTruncated` says when more exist); the ranking and every summary count use the complete set
`provenance` on a `dependencies` page is on the REPORT, not repeated per row
tools.performance: Every collection mode is a page and says so. `limit` bounds the answer — 25 edges per direction for callers/callees/trace (default), 20 files for dependencies, 50 entries for test_mapping/test_gaps, 50 files for test_quality. Measured warm (five runs, p50/p95, in validation/tools/bb_analyze/LATENCY.json): on a 5-file fixture every default mode answers in under 60 ms; on a 97-file synthetic index under 404 ms. On this workspace's reference index (6,452 files, 310,423 symbols, 820,040 relationships) stats answers in 5.2/7.4 s, complexity 2.8/2.9 s, test_quality 0.16/0.31 s, and the graph modes are bounded by a declared 2,000 ms walk ceiling that a single SQL statement can exceed — callers answered 11.0/12.4 s and callees 29.3/64.0 s on that index under fleet load. Default payloads on the reference index: stats 6.2 KB, complexity 5.4 KB, callers (hub) 33.6 KB, dependencies 203.8 KB, test_mapping 66.1 KB, test_quality 73.1 KB. A caller who wants less passes `limit` where the mode accepts it. The graph walk is additionally bounded by depth, per-node site limit, fan-out budget, and the wall-clock budget; whichever fires is named in `truncationReason`.
tools.safety: Read-only. Analysis never creates tests or edits source.
tools.evidence: Findings derive from brain_* symbols, files, relationships, complexity, and test-file classifications. `provenance.evidenceClass` classifies what kind of claim the answer is; `unknowns` names every absence the answer rests on.

tools.name: bb_doc
tools.description: Generate read-only, evidence-backed documentation with resolvable citations and a freshness block over the cited files. Every mode emits its declared section set, an empty result is never reported as passing, and the output budget is enforced on the payload the caller receives: `quality.budget.estimatedTokens` is measured on the decorated answer, and `estimatedTokens * 4` is never smaller than what was sent. When the required sections cannot fit, the result says so rather than dropping one. `quality.references` counts the citations the answer EMITS (plus the `collected*` totals of everything gathered), so the stale/missing numbers match the Sources list. Supports symbol, file, module, feature, API, project, and documentation-coverage modes in Markdown or JSON. When the cited files are stale, the handler auto-refreshes exactly those files within the shared budget and regenerates the document; refresh=false opts out and answers from existing data with the freshness block. A module target that matches no indexed file is refused by name rather than answered with project-wide facts, and `limit`/`maxTokens` outside their ranges are refused rather than clamped.

target.description: symbol, file, module, feature, or API target (`symbol`/`symbolName`/`query` are accepted as aliases); optional for project and coverage. `symbol` matches an indexed name, qualified name or its last dotted/`::` segment. `file` accepts an exact repository-relative path, an absolute path, a directory prefix, or a bare file name with or without its extension. `module` needs a repository-relative directory the index holds; a target that matches nothing is REFUSED with the forms tried. `project` accepts a target but uses it as document metadata only — it does not scope the selection.

audience.description: documentation audience: selects OPTIONAL sections only; a required section is never dropped for a smaller audience

detail.description: detail level: `brief` caps each section at 5 facts and drops optional sections, `standard` caps at `limit`, `deep` caps at 3x`limit` and adds the optional all-edges section; for `feature` it also enables semantic candidate expansion, which is much slower

includeExamples.description: include source-backed examples. No example is emitted when no cited snippet or verified contract supplies one; an honest not-observed unknown is recorded instead

includeDiagrams.description: include cited diagrams when available. This implementation does not emit diagrams; `reference.diagrams` stays empty and an honest not-observed unknown is recorded

includeTests.description: include indexed test evidence. Accepted for `symbol` and `feature` modes only (their documents render a test section); the other modes REFUSE it because it would do nothing. Absent means the mode default (on); explicit false suppresses the test facts

limit.description: maximum evidence items per section (whole number 1-100, default 20). Out-of-range values are REFUSED, not clamped, so the page returned is the page requested

maxTokens.description: output token budget measured on the emitted payload (whole number 1-16000, default 8000; the default clears the measured minimum honest rendering on the reference index, ~6,700 tokens). `estimatedTokens` reports that measurement; when the required sections cannot fit, `budget.passed` is false and a shortfall unknown names the smallest honest rendering. Out-of-range values are REFUSED

refresh.description: false opts out of the inline auto-refresh of the files this document cites (default: auto-refresh those files within the shared budget, then regenerate); the decision is always declared in `autoRefresh` or the answer text

documentation.summary: Cited Markdown or JSON documentation over indexed source and relationships, with declared bounds, emitted-citation freshness counts, and a payload-measured output budget.

returns: Markdown or structured JSON documentation: title, summary, the mode's declared sections, citation objects with stable IDs and per-citation freshness, and declared unknowns

`quality`: the four-term verdict, emitted-citation reference counts (`broken`/`stale`/`missing` plus the `collectedStale`/`collectedMissing` totals of everything gathered), completeness against the declared section set, the index snapshot, and the payload-measured budget
`quality.bounds`: per-section numbers — `available`, `capped`, `droppedForBudget`, `emitted` — with `emitted + droppedForBudget === capped` enforced before the result is returned
A declared selection bound when a scope has more indexed symbols than the evidence limit selected, naming both numbers
`reference`: stable website keys (`projectId`, `snapshotId`, `generatedAt`, `indexVersion`, `schemaVersion`, `sourceLanguage`, `canonicalPath`, `slugs`, `tags`) and an empty `diagrams` array
An `autoRefresh` line whenever stale cited files were repaired or a repair was declined, with the reason
errors: Missing mode, or a mode outside symbol|file|module|feature|api|project|coverage
Missing target for `symbol`, `file`, `module` or `feature`
`limit` outside 1-100, or `maxTokens` outside 1-16000 — refused with the accepted range rather than clamped
`includeTests` on a mode that renders no test evidence (everything except `symbol` and `feature`)
A `module` target that matches no indexed file — refused by name, with the two directory forms it tried
