path.description: optional file path to scope the note to one file's copy of the symbol, max 1024 chars; resolved to the index's own spelling (`brain_file.relative_path`), so `src/a.ts`, `./src/a.ts` and the absolute path all reach the same note

toolIdentity.description: optional name of the calling agent/tool, max 200 chars (recorded verbatim; line breaks and control characters are refused)

documentation.summary: Agent note with enforced provenance, stored where the human reads.

examples.body: Legacy auth path — scheduled for removal in Q3.

returns: The stored annotation row with its enforced provenance (`author_class` is always `agent` for tool writes) and the caller's self-declared `toolIdentity`, recorded verbatim with `time_created`/`time_updated`

`replaced` — present only when this location already held a different note: the previous author class, tool identity, body and timestamps, so the second writer can merge instead of clobbering. The previous note does not survive in the store

`surfacing` — a MEASUREMENT against the index, not a promise: `editor` (bool, the JOINT truth — the name or qualified name must be indexed AND declared in the resolved file), `nameMatched`, `pathMatched`, `fileMatched` (`true`/`false` when a path was given, `null` for a name-level note), `matchedAs` (`name` and/or `qualifiedName`), `matchedNames`, and a `statement` saying what is and is not true. A name that is indexed only in a DIFFERENT file than the one the path resolves to is reported `editor: false` with that reason — the hover and graph badge select notes by the file under the cursor, so those two individually-true halves would render nowhere

The path handling: `surfacing.pathNote` when a path was resolved to the index's own spelling, `surfacing.pathWarning` when no indexed file matches the given path (stored under that spelling, no editor surface will scope it to a file), and a name-level note statement when no path was given
errors: Missing or blank symbol
Symbol longer than the declared 500-char limit — refused, never truncated
Empty or whitespace-only body (a refusal, not a silent no-op)
Body longer than the declared 2000-char limit, counted in characters (an astral glyph is one character, not two UTF-16 units)
Path longer than the declared 1024-char limit — refused, never truncated
toolIdentity longer than the declared 200-char limit — refused, never truncated

toolIdentity containing a control character or line break — a label is a name, not a document. Refused, because a line break in that field is exactly what once rendered as a SECOND provenance line that could claim to be a human note
Unknown options (including `author_class`/`authorClass`) are rejected by name with the accepted option list — provenance is not a caller input
limitations: Annotations are opinions layered on index evidence, never index truth
Any symbol name is accepted. Reachability is reported, not enforced: a name no indexed symbol carries is stored and declared `surfacing.editor: false`
The note is keyed on the name as given. A name that matches several indexed symbols is one name-level note shown wherever that name appears, unless `path` scopes it to a file

`surfacing.editor` is the joint rule the editors apply: the symbol must be declared in the file the path resolves to (or the note must be name-level). A name match plus a path match for a different file is reported `editor: false`

`path` is resolved to the index's own spelling (`brain_file.relative_path`), so `src/a.ts`, `./src/a.ts` and the absolute path are the SAME note. A path matching no indexed file is stored verbatim and declared
`toolIdentity` is the caller's own label. It is recorded verbatim and never verified — `author_class` is the enforced field

The editor renderer escapes EVERY interpolated field, not only the body: `author_class`, `tool_identity` and `body` all go through the escaper, and a line break in any of them is flattened to a space, so one stored row always renders as one line. Markup escaping alone is not enough — a newline is what turns one annotation into two in a markdown list

One note is kept per author per location, so a second agent annotating the same symbol+path REPLACES the first note. The replacement is reported in `replaced` with the previous body, but the previous note does not survive in the store. Annotating a DIFFERENT path (or no path) keeps a separate note per location
On a project that has never been indexed, the first write creates that project's annotation store; the reply still reports `surfacing.editor: false` because no symbol can be matched yet
This tool does not report per-file index staleness and does not auto-refresh: output reflects the index as of the last index run
tools.performance: Measured through the real MCP stdio door on isolated indexes, five warm runs per tier (validation/tools/bb_annotate/LATENCY.json): p50 83.4 / p95 96.1 ms on the 5-file polyglot fixture; p50 5.8 / p95 12.1 ms on the 97-file n100 fixture; p50 5.7 / p95 17.9 ms on the 564-file graphql-js corpus; p50 3.5 / p95 5.1 ms on the 109-file rake corpus; p50 3.8 / p95 5.8 ms on the 6,452-file / 310,423-symbol reference index. The first call in a fresh server process opens the project index read-write and runs its additive migrations, measured at 1.8 s on the reference-index snapshot. The write itself is three indexed lookups (name, qualified name, file row) plus the location upsert.
tools.safety: Write-capable against the annotation store only. It never modifies source files. It opens the project index read-write the way every write door does, so the additive schema migrations may apply on the first call; index content outside brain_annotation is not written.
tools.evidence: Provenance is enforced three ways: the write hardcodes 'agent', the column is NOT NULL, and a storage trigger constrains `author_class` to {agent, human} — so a row cannot carry a third claim that every reader would render verbatim. `toolIdentity` and timestamps are recorded, and the toolIdentity claim is a label, not evidence. Reachability is measured against the same predicates the readers use: `brain_symbol.name`/`qualified_name` for the name, `brain_file.relative_path` for the file.

tools.name: bb_annotations
tools.description: Read annotations for a symbol, one file's copy of a symbol (optional `path`), or all annotations up to the declared limit, with full provenance on every row: author class, tool identity, and timestamps. Every answer declares its bound: `count` is the page size, `totalCountIfKnown` the true total, and `truncated`/`truncationReason` fire when the limit actually dropped rows — a short page is never mistaken for a complete one. A `symbol` also matches notes written under a symbol's qualified name, the same predicate the editor uses. No annotations is a declared absence, never an error. To write a note use bb_annotate.

symbol.description: symbol name (omit to list all annotations); `target`/`query` are accepted as aliases

path.description: optional file path; resolved to the index's own spelling first, so `src/a.ts`, `./src/a.ts` and the absolute path are the same note. Returns that file's copy's notes plus any name-level notes (written with no path). Omit to return every note for the symbol

includeNameLevel.description: with `path` and no `symbol`, also return name-level notes (written with no path), which apply wherever their name appears. Off by default, so a path filter answers the question as asked rather than mixing in the whole project

documentation.summary: Annotations with full provenance; absence declared.

returns: Typed annotations for a symbol or the whole project, with full provenance on every row (author class, tool identity, timestamps)

`count` (the page size), `totalCountIfKnown` (the true number of matching annotations) and `truncated` with a `truncationReason` naming the fix — a bounded read declares its bound, like bb_search and bb_graph. This door used to return only `count`, so a project with 300 notes and the default limit answered a flat `count: 50` with no way to know 250 more existed
Declared-absent result when none exist — absence is never an error
errors: limit outside the declared 1-200 range
limitations: Reads only stored annotations; absence is declared, not inferred
Annotation store semantics are owned by the M28 workstream
Without `path`, a symbol that lives in several files returns every file's notes together; pass `path` (or read each row's symbol_path) to separate them

A `symbol` filter also matches notes written under a symbol's QUALIFIED name, because that is one of the two name forms the editor accepts. This is the same predicate `surfacing` reports, so a reader and the editor always agree on which notes exist
`path` is resolved to the index's own spelling before filtering, so a reader passing `./src/a.ts` finds the note a writer stored as `src/a.ts`

A `path` filter WITHOUT a `symbol` returns that file's own notes only. It used to also return every NAME-LEVEL note in the project, because a name-level note does apply wherever its name appears — but that made a narrow question answer mostly-global: measured on a real corpus, a path read returned 2 notes for the file and 48 name-level notes from the whole project, and the file's own notes were nearly cut off by the default limit. Pass `includeNameLevel: true` for the broader set. With a `symbol` AND a `path`, name-level notes about THAT symbol are still included, because they are about the symbol you asked for
tools.performance: Indexed lookup by project and symbol (brain_annotation_project_symbol_idx). The declared total is a second COUNT over the same predicate, so `totalCountIfKnown` costs one indexed count.
tools.safety: Read-only. It does not modify source files, index data, or annotations.
tools.evidence: Rows come from brain_annotation with provenance fields preserved.
